claims.claim: The two source-stated bounds imply total update time Õ(min{n²,m^(4/3)}). This meets Õ(n√m) when m≤n^(6/5) and when m≥n²/log^{O(1)}n; over all m it is within an Õ(n^(1/4)) factor of the target.
claims.evidence: The sparse-bound ratio to the target is m^(4/3)/(n√m)=m^(5/6)/n, giving the exact threshold m≤n^(6/5). The dense-bound ratio is n/√m, which is polylogarithmic when m≥n²/log^C n. The two polynomial bounds cross at m=n^(3/2), where both ratios equal n^(1/4), and the ratio is monotone toward that crossing from either side.
claims.witness: Writing m=n^a gives ratio exponents 5a/6−1 for a≤3/2 and 1−a/2 for a≥3/2; their common maximum is 1/4 at a=3/2.
claims.search_method: Independent symbolic exponent comparison, followed by exact rational-arithmetic checks.

claims.claim: Reachability-rectangle identity: if R is reflexive reachability immediately before inserting u→v, A={x:xRu}, D={y:vRy}, and R⁺ is reachability afterward, then R⁺=R∪(A×D). Hence an insertion sequence evolves reachability exactly by monotone union with these time-dependent ancestor–descendant rectangles.
claims.evidence: Any newly reachable off-diagonal pair has a simple post-insertion path using u→v exactly once; splitting there gives an old path to u and an old path from v. Conversely, concatenating those two old paths with u→v realizes every pair in A×D. Reflexive pairs were already in R, so cycles and self-loops introduce no exception.
claims.witness: Exact bitset closure confirmed the identity for all 502,170 backward-edge insertions into all 33,866 DAGs compatible with orders of size at most six.
claims.search_method: Proved both relation inclusions and exhaustively searched all small ordered DAGs.

claims.claim: Corrected balanced-cut lemma: for every order-violating insertion u→v into a DAG, either v already reaches u, so the insertion closes a cycle, or one can find equally sized sets B,F and a cut c such that F consists of the descendants of v at or left of c, B consists of the ancestors of u right of c, the stable order (L\F),B,F,(R\B) is topological after the insertion, and all |B||F| ordered pairs in B×F become newly reachable.
claims.evidence: In the acyclic branch, D(v) and A(u) are disjoint. Sweeping a cut from before v to before u, h=|D∩L|−|A∩R| starts negative, ends nonnegative, and increases only by zero or one, so it attains zero after v has entered L and the common size is positive. All potentially reversed old-edge types in the four-block reorder are excluded by descendant closure, ancestor closure, the old topological order, or the absence of a v-to-u path. Each b∈B reaches each f∈F through the new edge, while their reverse old-order positions prove the pair was previously unreachable.
claims.witness: All 176,765 acyclic order-violating cases on ordered DAGs of size at most six had a nonempty balanced cut; every such cut tested produced a valid new topological order and fresh B×F pairs.
claims.search_method: Sweep-invariant proof, exhaustive edge-type analysis, and exhaustive finite counterexample search.

claims.claim: Structural reduction for the balanced-cut route: suppose a combinatorial ordered-reachability boundary oracle can absorb all edge insertions and stable block reorders in total Õ(n+m+Σ_i q_i) time, and on each violating insertion either reports an old v-to-u path or returns a cut c with F=D(v)∩L_c, B=A(u)∩R_c, and |B|=|F|=q_i>0. Then it yields an incremental topological-sort algorithm with total update time Õ(n√m).
claims.evidence: The balanced-cut lemma makes every returned reorder correct. Each update charges q_i² distinct ordered pairs that become reachable for the first time, so monotonicity gives Σq_i²≤n(n−1). With at most m charged updates, Cauchy–Schwarz yields Σq_i≤√(mΣq_i²)=O(n√m). Balanced-sequence-tree work is soft-linear in Σq_i; for a simple directed graph, n+m and one terminal O(n)-length cycle certificate are also within O(n√m) when m≥1.
claims.witness: The exact charging certificate is (Σq_i)²≤mΣq_i²≤mn(n−1). The claim is correctly conditional: it does not assert that the stipulated oracle has been constructed.
claims.search_method: Checked the conditional dependencies, freshness charging, Cauchy–Schwarz step, and all additive costs independently.

claims.claim: The balanced-cut construction gives an explicit combinatorial algorithm with total time Õ(m+n√m+A), where A is the total number of adjacency entries scanned from selected forward vertices and selected backward vertices. Consequently it attains Õ(n√m) whenever A=Õ(n√m), including sequences in which every selected forward vertex has polylogarithmic out-degree and every selected backward vertex has polylogarithmic in-degree at its expansion time.
claims.evidence: A min-heap forward traversal enumerates descendants in old topological order, and a max-heap backward traversal enumerates ancestors in reverse order. Expanding one vertex on each side until the unexpanded frontiers cross produces equal-size exact boundary sets; if a v-to-u path exists, the discovered searches intersect before a cut is returned. Heap insertions and inspections are charged to scanned adjacency entries, stable reordering costs Õ(q_i), and the fresh-pair argument bounds Σq_i by O(n√m). Under the stated degree condition, A is polylogarithmic times the number of selected vertices, namely Õ(Σq_i+n) including the sole terminal cycle search.
claims.witness: The checker implemented the paired heap-frontier algorithm and obtained the correct cycle-or-cut result on all 502,170 small ordered-DAG violations, including 325,405 cycle-forming cases.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed and proved the heap stopping invariant, audited every cost category, and exhaustively tested the search.

claims.claim: The rectangle reformulation cannot be implemented by eagerly materializing every newly reachable pair within the target bound: there is an insertion sequence with n=2r and m=2r−1 whose final insertion creates exactly r² new reachability pairs. Thus any implementation doing Ω(1) work per newly created pair takes Ω(n²), not Õ(n√m), on this sequence.
claims.evidence: Before joining the two disjoint r-vertex chains, no first-chain vertex reaches a second-chain vertex. Inserting the edge from the first sink to the second source creates every one of the r² cross-chain pairs and no other new pair. Here n√m=Θ(r^(3/2)), whereas eager per-pair work is Θ(r²), whose ratio Θ(√r) is not polylogarithmic.
claims.witness: The construction has exactly 2(r−1)+1=2r−1 edges and exactly r² fresh pairs; exact closure checks succeeded for every 2≤r≤64.
claims.search_method: Direct symbolic counting plus exact transitive-closure checks across a parameter range.

claims.claim: Full adjacency-list rescanning cannot be charged automatically to the balanced-search vertex bound: there is a DAG sequence with n=2r+2 and m=4r in which every violating update has q=1 and creates exactly one new reachability pair, yet rescanning the selected forward list costs r².
claims.evidence: With edges v→w_j, z→w_j, and u_i→z installed first, inserting u_i→v moves u_i immediately before v. At that update the relevant cut has F={v} and B={u_i}; u_i already reaches z and every w_j, so only (u_i,v) is newly reachable. Nevertheless, a full expansion of v scans its same r outgoing entries on each of the r violations.
claims.witness: There are 3r initial edges, r violating insertions, 2r+2 vertices, and r·r forward-list scans. Exact simulations succeeded for 1≤r≤32.
claims.search_method: Stepwise reconstruction of the maintained order and exact closure comparison before and after every insertion.

claims.claim: Semantically, the balanced search may be restricted to the old topological interval [v,u]: ignoring forward neighbors after u and backward neighbors before v preserves cycle detection and produces the same descendant/ancestor intersections needed by every cut between v and u.
claims.evidence: Positions strictly increase along every nontrivial old-DAG path. Therefore every v-to-u path lies wholly in [v,u]; likewise, a path from v to a vertex left of a cut cannot leave the interval and return, and a path from a vertex right of the cut to u cannot first go before v. Thus restricted searches recover exactly the needed D(v)∩L_c and A(u)∩R_c sets.
claims.witness: For all 502,170 tested violations, closure in the induced interval agreed with unrestricted closure on both relevant intersections and on the v-to-u cycle predicate.
claims.search_method: Path-position monotonicity proof and exhaustive induced-interval closure comparison.

claims.claim: Even perfect filtering of adjacency entries outside the active interval does not make full-list balanced expansion Õ(n√m): for every p,q≥2 there is a block-swap sequence on n=pq vertices and m=[pq(q−1)+p(p−1)]/2 edges with p(p−1)/2 violating updates, each having |B|=|F|=q, whose selected-block internal entries alone are rescanned p(p−1)q(q−1)/2 times. Setting p=q² gives m=Θ(n^(4/3)) and Θ(n²) scans, a Θ(n^(1/3)) factor above n√m.
claims.evidence: The nested adjacent-swap order is valid: before inserting the j-to-a block edge, C_a is immediately before C_j, all existing cross-block reachability points from larger indices to smaller ones, and no old C_a-to-C_j path exists. At the intervening cut the exact forward and backward sets are C_a and C_j. Their complete-DAG internal entries all lie inside [v,u], contributing q(q−1) scans per update. The stated edge, update, and scan totals follow by exact summation.
claims.witness: For p=q², n=q³, m=q⁴−(q³+q²)/2, and scans=q²(q²−1)q(q−1)/2=Θ(q⁶); hence n√m=Θ(q⁵) and the ratio is Θ(q)=Θ(n^(1/3)). Exact block simulations covered 2≤p≤7, 2≤q≤6 and p=q² for 2≤q≤4.
claims.search_method: Inductive block-order and reachability analysis, exact formula checking, and stepwise transitive-closure simulation.

target_evidence: The draft does not prove the full source target. Claim 3 assumes an ordered-reachability boundary oracle with the required total cost, and claim 4 retains an uncontrolled scan term A; claim 8 gives valid sequences where that implementation has A=Θ(n²) while n√m=Θ(n^(5/3)). The balanced-cut lemma, conditional reduction, restricted-degree result, and obstruction families are nevertheless correct and material partial progress. The draft explicitly labels itself PARTIAL and states that the arbitrary-degree intermediate-density case remains unresolved.
